skill.name: ticktick-cli
skill.description: Manage Dida365 and TickTick projects and tasks through a Python CLI that calls the Dida365 Open API.
skill.summary: Control TickTick projects and tasks from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code with a Python CLI.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, API documentation fields, and normal UTF-8 README content. Confirmed risk remains because the skill performs authenticated network requests to Dida365 and directs OAuth setup through an author-controlled worker URL. No prompt-injection text was found in the scanned files.

remediation.issue: Author-controlled OAuth endpoint is used by default.
remediation.suggestion: Make the authorize URL and redirect URI configurable, and document a self-hosted worker deployment path for users.

remediation.issue: Bearer tokens and task data are sent to the configured API base URL.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before changing the base URL, and consider restricting token-bearing requests to trusted Dida365 endpoints by default.

remediation.issue: Delete commands do not require confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit confirmation step or a force flag for project and task deletion commands.

remediation.issue: OAuth callback does not validate state before returning an access token.
remediation.suggestion: Store and validate state for the OAuth flow, or clearly document that the helper is only for trusted single-user deployments.

content.user_title: Manage TickTick Tasks from the CLI
content.value_statement: Manual task updates slow scripted workflows. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code manage Dida365 tasks through a Python CLI.
actual_capabilities: Lists projects and retrieves project details, including tasks and kanban columns.
Creates, updates, and deletes Dida365 projects through CLI commands.
Creates, updates, completes, deletes, and reads tasks by project and task ID.
Supports checklist items through repeated item arguments or an item JSON input.
Outputs either formatted tables or JSON for agent-friendly automation.
Uses OAuth bearer tokens from a command option or environment variable.
limitations: Requires a valid Dida365 or TickTick OAuth access token before API calls work.
Sends task and project data to the configured Dida365 API endpoint.
Delete commands do not include an interactive confirmation prompt.
Search and jq-style filtering are planned but not implemented in this version.

use_cases.title: Automate Project Setup
use_cases.description: Create a project and seed tasks from an AI-assisted workflow without opening the TickTick app.

use_cases.title: Review Task State
use_cases.description: List projects, inspect task details, and export structured task data for status checks.

use_cases.title: Maintain Checklists
use_cases.description: Update checklist-style tasks for episodes, chapters, releases, or repeated production steps.

prompt_templates.title: List My Projects
prompt_templates.prompt: List my TickTick projects using the CLI. Show a concise table with IDs and names.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a task in my target project with this title, due date, and priority. Confirm the created task details.

prompt_templates.title: Update Checklist Items
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this existing task with the checklist items I provide. Use JSON output so I can verify each item.

prompt_templates.title: Plan And Apply Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this project, identify stale tasks, then propose updates before changing or deleting anything.

output_examples.output: A table of project IDs, names, colors, view modes, and sort order values.

output_examples.input: Create a task with three checklist items in a project.
output_examples.output: A confirmation showing the new task title, project ID, task ID, and checklist item titles.

output_examples.input: Complete a task by project ID and task ID.
output_examples.output: A short success message after the Dida365 API accepts the completion request.

best_practices: Use JSON output when another agent or script will consume the result.
Store OAuth tokens in environment variables instead of prompts or shared notes.
Review project and task IDs before running update, complete, or delete commands.
anti_patterns: Do not paste long-lived OAuth tokens into public chat logs or issue trackers.
Do not run delete commands without first retrieving the target project or task.
Do not point the base URL to an untrusted server while using a real access token.

faq.question: Does this skill require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It calls the Dida365 Open API and needs outbound HTTPS access.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: The CLI reads an OAuth access token from a command option or the TICKTICK_TOKEN environment variable.

faq.question: Can it create and delete data?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create, update, complete, and delete projects or tasks when the token has permission.

faq.question: Can it return machine-readable output?
faq.answer: Yes. Use JSON output when another tool needs to parse project or task data.

faq.question: Does it support checklist tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can pass checklist items through repeated item options or an item JSON input.

faq.question: Is the OAuth worker required?
faq.answer: No. It is a helper for obtaining tokens, and users should prefer their own trusted deployment.
